transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Mrs. Kowalski, thank you for meeting with me. I need to share some information with you regarding your care and the plan for your surgery.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you, Doctor. I have been praying a lot that everything will be handled in God's hands. I just want to be sure I'm doing the right thing by my family.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I appreciate you sharing that. I want to start by saying that I am very sorry. I am personally responsible for a mistake that was made regarding your imaging.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A mistake? What do you mean? Is something wrong with my heart?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: There was some confusion with the files and things didn't go quite right with how the images were stored.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't understand. Confusion? Please, just tell me what happened to me. I feel a great heaviness in my chest just hearing you say that.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know this is upsetting. I can see that you are feeling overwhelmed right now. I am truly sorry that we let this happen. It was my responsibility to ensure the correct images were reviewed, and I failed to do that.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But why? How does a doctor fail at something so simple? I trusted the Lord to lead me to this hospital, and now you tell me there is confusion?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It was a failure on my part. I take full accountability for this. I am deeply sorry for the distress this is causing you.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just feel so small in this big building. You all have your charts and your machines, but I am a human being. I just wanted to feel safe in your care.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is completely understandable that you feel vulnerable and let down.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to know exactly what happened. Did you give me the wrong medicine? Did you do a procedure on the wrong part of my body?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, nothing has been done to your body yet. There was just an issue with the accession numbers in the system.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: What is an accession number? Why are you using these words? Just tell me in plain English what happened to my scans.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: My apologies. We had a problem with the way the files were labeled.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not an answer. Are you saying you looked at someone else's pictures?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We had an issue with the organization of the studies.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: This is not helping me. I can feel my heart racing. I need to know if the surgery is still the right thing to do or if you have been planning the wrong surgery because you were looking at someone else!

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to get to the ward in a few minutes, so let's just focus on the fact that we are fixing it now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are rushing me! I am sitting here trembling and you are looking at your watch. Do you not care that I am frightened?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I do care. I really do. And I am sorry again for the mistake.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It is not just about the mistake, it is about how you are treating me right now. I feel like I am just a number to you, just like that number you mentioned.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I apologize. I am truly sorry for the error and for how I am handling this conversation. I take full responsibility for the mistake with the files.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So what happens now? Do I still have to have this operation?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We are going to re-review everything.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When? How do I know it will be right this time?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll look into it and we will let you know.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: That is not a plan. That is a guess. Who is going to tell me? When will I know?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Someone from the team will reach out to you soon.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Soon is not a time. I cannot go home and pray for a "soon." I need a day, a time, a name.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I will make sure you get an update eventually.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like I am drifting in a storm and you are not throwing me a rope.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am sorry. I really am.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language by stating 'I have to get to the ward in a few minutes' while the patient is in distress.

E.justification: Resident uses platitudes like 'things didn't go quite right' and 'confusion with the files' and fails to explicitly name the error despite patient's repeated requests.

A.justification: Resident uses direct apology language and repeatedly takes full personal accountability without deflection.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('overwhelmed', 'vulnerable', 'let down') and references the patient's feeling of being 'small'.

T.justification: Resident provides only placeholders ('we'll look into it', 'reach out to you soon', 'eventually') with no specific timeline or concrete plan.
